title: Unfenced 3PC or 2PC Under Network Partition Assumptions
pattern: A transaction manager or cohort implementation that makes unilateral commit or abort decisions purely based on time-based timeouts during network communication silences, without establishing a verified quorum or barrier fence.
why_bad: Two-Phase Commit (2PC) blocks cohorts on coordinator failure to preserve safety [64, 184]. While Three-Phase Commit (3PC) attempts to remove this blocking behavior via timeouts, it relies on a synchronous timing assumption [64, 184]. Under network partitions (common in asynchronous networks), some cohorts can communicate with the coordinator while others cannot [64]. Deciding to commit or abort based on local timeouts leads to a split-brain condition where nodes on one side commit and nodes on the other abort, permanently corrupting database consistency [64, 184].
detection: Identify error handlers or timeout handlers in distributed transaction engines (e.g., implementing 2PC, 3PC protocols) that execute hard commit commands unilaterally when a remote coordinator or participant request times out.
fix: Do not use raw timeout-based commitment protocols under asynchronous network models. Implement consensus-based replication or coordinate distributed commits via a persistent, replicated state log (such as Raft or Paxos) to guarantee atomic agreement [68, 183, 190].
source: Alex Petrov, *Database Internals*, Chapter 13 (Consensus and 3PC) / passages [63, 64, 68]; Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*, Chapter 9 / passages [183, 184, 190].
